transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-25
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Elliot (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Markus (NovaCare - Sec Eng), Priya (NovaCare - Cloud Architect), Dana (NovaCare - Head Eng), Luis (NovaCare - Platform)

Summary: quick security review focused on SSO/SAML + SCIM provisioning and RBAC. Questions about least-privilege, audit log retention, KMS / CMEK, and data residency. Action items captured at end.

[00:00] Samira: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call?
[00:04] Markus: hey this is markus, i'm on sec eng.
[00:06] Priya: priya here, cloud arch.
[00:07] Dana: dana - head of eng.
[00:09] Luis: luis platform.
[00:11] Samira: awesome, i've got elliot and jordan from our solutions team, they'll take point on the technical bits. quick agenda - SSO/SAML integration, SCIM provisioning, RBAC model and then logs/encryption questions. sound good?
[00:22] Priya: yep works.
[00:24] Elliot: cool. i'll start with our SAML flow and how attributes map, then jordan will cover SCIM.

[00:28] Elliot: so, Redwood supports IdPs that speak standard SAML 2.0 and we've got pre-built configs for Okta and Azure AD. you provide the IdP metadata XML and our console or support can upload and validate. the typical attributes we consume are: nameid (email), givenName, familyName, and groups (optional). we also support custom attributes if you need e.g. employee_id or tenant_id.
[00:52] Priya: for groups, do you expect the groups claim in the assertion or via SCIM sync? we currently do group-based entitlements in okta.
[00:58] Jordan: good q. you can do either but recommended pattern is SCIM for group provisioning so you get canonical group membership and deprovisioning. we accept groups in SAML for quick role mapping but that's more brittle.
[01:12] Markus: what's your recommendation for least-privilege roles? we want fine-grained control but not 50 roles to manage.
[01:18] Elliot: we typically suggest a small set of roles: Admin (full), Operator (deploy/manage routes), Viewer (read only), ApiService (service accounts with token-limited scope). then you can use group-to-role mapping in SCIM to map Okta groups to those roles. customers that need more granularity add role-scoped permissions.
[01:36] Dana: do you support JIT provisioning on SAML or does SCIM handle that?
[01:40] Jordan: JIT for SAML is supported for basic user creation if you embed the right attributes, but SCIM is the recommended for robust lifecycle: create, update, deactivate. SCIM also supports group push.
[01:52] Luis: any limitations on SCIM? like custom group attributes or large orgs?
[01:56] Jordan: SCIM endpoints are rate-limited slightly for provisioning bursts but we have high throughput plans for Dedicated customers. for large orgs we recommend a one-time bulk sync then incremental SCIM changes. there are known quirks in some IdPs where nested groups flatten differently - okta flattens nested groups sometimes, we document these.

[02:15] Priya: about audit logs - what events do you retain and for how long? we feed logs into our SIEM (Splunk).
[02:22] Elliot: by default we retain 90 days of detailed audit logs in the console. enterprise packages can extend retention; we can stream logs to your SIEM via syslog/HTTPS forwarding or ship to your cloud storage (S3/GCS) with lifecycle policies. events include sign-in, token issuance, API key creation, role changes, SCIM provisioning events, model access logs (metadata only, we don't log full prompt content unless you enable debug tracing).
[02:48] Markus: do you log assertion attributes or sensitive fields?
[02:52] Elliot: we mask sensitive fields in logs; we do not persist raw SAML assertions by default. we can keep a hashed reference for troubleshooting. if you need full traces for an incident, that requires an explicit enablement and is recorded with stricter access controls.
[03:06] Dana: encryption and KMS - can we bring our own key? we need CMEK for regulatory reasons.
[03:12] Elliot: yes, we support customer-managed keys in our Private and Dedicated offerings; for Hosted we have CCM (customer-controlled keys) in some regions. we integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM-backed KMS via standard APIs. keys can be rotated; we support key rotation with a seamless re-wrap flow.
[03:30] Priya: ok and data residency - we need EU residency for some PHI-like metadata. how do you guarantee residency?
[03:36] Jordan: we have region pinning on our Private/Dedicated plans where data storage and control plane can be restricted to specific cloud regions. we also provide an on-prem deployment for air-gapped scenarios. for hosted API, we offer EU regions and residency controls via contract-level SLA but not the same guarantee as private.
[03:55] Markus: in terms of SSO user lifecycle, how do you handle deprovisioning latency if someone is removed in Okta? we want immediate lockout.
[04:02] Jordan: SCIM deactivation is near real-time; typical propagation under 30s for most IdPs, barring IdP throttling. if you rely solely on SAML without SCIM, we'd recommend combining it with session TTLs and a short re-auth window.
[04:18] Luis: what about service accounts and API keys - how do they factor into RBAC?
[04:22] Elliot: service accounts are first-class: generate tokens tied to an org role with adjustable TTLs. we encourage short-lived tokens and automatic rotation. API keys are scoped and auditable; you can bind them to specific models, routes, or usage quotas.
[04:36] Dana: can we enforce RBAC for the console UI vs API separately?
[04:39] Elliot: yes, roles are policy-based and you can scope permissions to console actions vs API actions; e.g., someone can be a "billing viewer" but not be able to create API keys.

[04:50] Priya: about SCIM mapping - can you map Okta groups to multiple roles or only one-to-one?
[04:55] Jordan: you can do both. mapping rules support multiple target roles and you can add conditionals on attributes. we provide a UI mapping tool and a JSON mapping file if you want to manage in IaC.
[05:08] Markus: any gotchas with Azure AD? we've seen claims truncation with some providers.
[05:12] Elliot: yeah azure sometimes truncates long group lists in the SAML assertion; that's another reason to use SCIM. also check SAML NameID format - we prefer email but can accept persistent IDs.

[05:26] Samira: want to cover audit logging delivery options quickly?
[05:29] Elliot: sure - 1) Console log retention (90d by default) 2) Push to customer SIEM via HTTPS or syslog 3) Export to cloud storage where you manage lifecycle 4) Real-time event stream (Kafka or webhook) for Dedicated/Private. all include event types and metadata; we don't include PII text of prompts unless enabled.
[05:51] Priya: webhooks - are they signed? we need to verify authenticity.
[05:54] Jordan: yes, webhooks are HMAC-signed and we recommend validating signature and timestamp to guard replay attacks.

[06:03] Luis: about incident response - will Redwood provide audit trails for investigations?
[06:07] Elliot: yes, we can provide an immutable audit trail and SRM logs; for enterprise customers we can also provide time-bound forensic exports and collaborate under an NDA.

[06:18] Dana: ok so next, SCIM group membership attributes - do you support custom meta like department/role for RBAC conditions?
[06:24] Jordan: yup custom attributes are supported in SCIM; you can use them in mapping conditions. example: if department=="billing" and group=="ops" then map to operator role.

[06:36] [small cross-talk: inaudible]

[06:40] Priya: curious about SAML certificate rotation - how seamless is rotating the IdP cert?
[06:45] Elliot: you can upload new IdP cert and schedule a swap window. we support dual-cert validation for a short overlap period. for SP-initiated flows we also support automatic metadata refresh if your IdP publishes metadata endpoint.

[06:58] Markus: about compliance: do you have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001? any relevant reports?
[07:04] Samira: yes we are SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified; i'll drop the latest attestation and our security whitepaper.
[07:10] Markus: great will want to redline the BAA for PHI considerations.
[07:13] Dana: can you confirm data at rest encryption scope - is model cache considered sensitive?
[07:18] Elliot: caches can store KV cache metadata; by default those are encrypted at rest. we recommend private/dedicated for workloads with strict PHI because we also offer control over KMS.

[07:30] Priya: latency of SCIM provisioning - do you have SLA?
[07:33] Jordan: not SLA'd for SCIM granular latency on hosted, but for Dedicated we can include provisioning SLOs. normal behaviour is under a minute.

[07:42] Samira: any questions about RBAC defaults?
[07:45] Markus: how do you handle cross-organization guests? contractors that need limited access?
[07:50] Elliot: support for guest accounts via SCIM/IdP groups. you can set tighter TTLs and session revocation policies for guest-role mappings. additionally you can place them in separate org-scoped projects with narrower permissions.

[08:03] Priya: one more Q: can SCIM sync include custom LDAP attributes? we're syncing from an LDAP-backed IdP.
[08:09] Jordan: yes, as long as your IdP exposes them via SCIM provisioning connector. some LDAP->SCIM bridges exist; we'll help validate mapping.

[08:22] Dana: talk to me about emergency access / break glass.
[08:25] Elliot: we have a break-glass flow: an audit-logged emergency token generation with multi-step approvals (can be integrated with your approval workflow). tokens are time-limited and flagged in logs.

[08:38] Markus: for the test we want to provision a test Okta tenant and try group->role mapping, then simulate deprovisioning. what's the easiest path?
[08:45] Samira: ideal is you provision a staging Okta tenant, add a few test users and groups, share the metadata XML, and we'll configure on our side and run a short onboarding with Elliot and Jordan. we'll also provide a runbook.

[09:00] Priya: about logging again - do you offer redaction rules for logs? we don't want PHI in any logs.
[09:06] Elliot: yes you can set auto-redaction rules; we also have an option to disable debug-level capture. for hosted we default to redact PII and prompts; for private you can customize more.

[09:18] Samira: going to capture the key decisions: you'll provision test Okta, we will set up SCIM mapping and short TTLs for sessions, we'll share SOC2 and KMS docs, and schedule follow up.

[09:32] [time jump / paraphrasing - discussion of token TTLs and API key scoping - inaudible sections]

[14:40] Jordan: one more note on attribute mapping - if you want to enforce org-level isolation, include a tenant_id claim in SAML and validate in our policy engine. it prevents cross-tenant elevation if someone is in multiple org groups.

[15:02] Priya: that tenant_id claim - okta can include it as a custom attribute. we'll test.

[15:10] Markus: are SCIM deletes soft-delete or hard-delete? we need to preserve audit trail.

[15:15] Elliot: soft-delete by default with an expiry; audit events include the delete event. for forensic needs we can capture a snapshot before purge.

[15:26] Dana: need clarity on role change propagation - when a user's role changes in Okta, how soon do permissions update?

[15:31] Jordan: near immediate via SCIM update, again depends on IdP push cadence. typical sub-30s with normal throughput.

[15:42] Priya: any RKMS/HSM vendor constraints? we use Vault + HSM-backed keys.

[15:47] Elliot: we have integrations with Vault via KMS plugins and can accept HSM-backed key material. we'll coordinate with your security ops for key wrapping policies.

[16:00] Markus: can we get an export of RBAC audit events separated by project? we need to feed into our compliance reports.

[16:05] Jordan: yes exports can be filtered by org/project and event type. we'll provide schema and sample extracts.

[16:18] [background noise - coffee truck?]

[16:22] Priya: just checking - are login sessions single sign-on across multiple orgs?
[16:26] Elliot: sessions are scoped to an org context; we don't silently elevate across org boundaries without re-auth.

[16:36] Samira: ok want to confirm action items and owners. i've put three items in the notes - runbook, logs schema, test tenant. anything else?

[16:45] Dana: can you include a sample RBAC matrix showing role->privilege mappings?

[16:48] Samira: yes will include RBAC matrix.

[16:52] Markus: for our legal folks will want the SOC2 and ISO packages plus BAA template.

[16:56] Samira: i'll send those under NDA link.

[17:00] Priya: timeline - we'd like POC in July, pilot with 50 users. is that feasible?

[17:06] Samira: yes july POC is feasible; we'll align resources once you hand over metadata.

[17:12] Luis: one operational Q - what's the expected outage window during SAML cert rotation?

[17:18] Jordan: with dual-cert overlap planned, zero downtime if done correctly; we'll help coordinate the window.

[17:28] [longer technical digression on token TTL and refresh tokens - paraphrased]

[22:45] Elliot: quick note - for Dedicated customers we can also put an inline policy engine so you can enforce attribute-based access control beyond just roles.

[22:56] Markus: that might be useful for our compliance rules.

[23:02] Samira: ok wrapping up - i'll email the runbook, elliot will send the logs schema, priya will share test tenant. schedule follow-up for next week for mapping deep dive.

[23:18] Priya: thanks all.

[23:20] Dana: thanks.

[23:21] Samira: thanks everyone, end.

End of transcript.
